translations.text: The Teaching of Addai the Apostle
The letter of King Abgar, son of King Manu, and when he sent it to our Lord in Jerusalem;
and when Addai the apostle came to him in Edessa, and what he said in proclaiming the good news;
and what he said and commanded as he was departing from this world, to those who had received ordination to the priesthood from him.
In the year three hundred and forty-three of the kingdom of the Greeks, during the reign of our lord Tiberius Caesar, the Roman,
and during the reign of King Abgar, son of King Manu, on the twelfth day of the month of First Tishri, Abgar the Black sent Marihab and Shamshagram,
leaders and dignitaries of his kingdom, and Hannan, the trusted archivist, with them, to the city called Eleutheropolis,
or Beth Guvrin in Aramaic, to the noble Sabinus, son of Eustorgius, the governor appointed by our lord Caesar,
who ruled over Syria, Phoenicia, Palestine, and the whole region of Mesopotamia.
They brought him letters concerning the affairs of the kingdom. When they came to him, he received them with joy
and honor. They stayed with him for twenty-five days, and he wrote them a reply to the letters
and sent them to King Abgar. When they left him, they traveled and came along the road toward Jerusalem.
They saw many people coming from far away to see Christ, because news of the wonders of his mighty deeds had spread
to distant lands. When Marihab, Shamshagram, and Hannan the archivist saw these people,
they too went with them to Jerusalem. When they entered Jerusalem, they saw Christ and rejoiced
with the crowds accompanying him. They also saw the Jews standing in groups
and considering what to do to him. For they were distressed to see that many of their own people believed in him.
They stayed there in Jerusalem for ten days, and Hannan the archivist wrote down
everything he saw Christ doing, as well as the other things he had done there before they arrived.
They set out and came to Edessa, and appeared before King Abgar, their lord, who had sent them.
They gave him the reply to the letters they had taken with them. After the letters had been read, they began to tell the king everything they had seen
and everything Christ had done in Jerusalem. Hannan the archivist read before him everything he had written
and brought with him. When King Abgar heard it, he was astonished and amazed, as were his nobles who stood before him.
Abgar said to them, “These mighty deeds are not human deeds, but God's, because no one can raise the dead except God alone.”
Abgar wanted to travel to Palestine himself and see with his own eyes everything Christ was doing.
And because he could not cross into Roman territory, which was not his own, lest this occasion provoke bitter hostility,
he wrote a letter and sent it to Christ through Hannan the archivist. Hannan left Edessa on the fourteenth of Adar
and entered Jerusalem on the twelfth of Nisan, a Wednesday. He found Christ at the house of Gamaliel, a leader of the Jews.
The letter was read before him. It was written as follows: “Abgar the Black, to Jesus, the good physician who has appeared in the region of Jerusalem:
My Lord, greetings. I have heard about you and your healing, that you heal not with medicines and roots,
but by your word you open the eyes of the blind, make the lame walk, cleanse lepers, and make the deaf hear.
By that same word of yours you heal those afflicted by spirits, epilepsy, and torment. You even raise the dead.
When I heard that you perform these great wonders, I concluded that either you are God, who has come down from heaven
and done these things, or you are the Son of God, since you do all these things. For this reason I have written to ask you
to come to me, as I worship you, and heal an illness I have, since I have put my faith in you.
I have also heard that the Jews are murmuring against you and persecuting you, and even want to crucify you
and are intent on harming you. I rule a city that is small and beautiful, and it is large enough for us both to live in peace.”
When Jesus received the letter at the house of the high priest of the Jews, he said to Hannan the archivist:
“Go and tell your master who sent you to me: Blessed are you, because you have believed in me without seeing me. For it is written about me
that those who see me will not believe in me, and those who do not see me will believe in me.
As for what you wrote to me, asking me to come to you, I am now released from the task for which I was sent here,
and I am going up to my Father who sent me. When I have gone up to him, I will send you one of my disciples
to heal the illness you have and make you well. He will turn everyone with you toward eternal life, and your city will be blessed.
No enemy will ever again gain power over it.” Now when Hannan the archivist saw that Jesus had spoken to him in this way,
since he was the king’s painter, he took and painted a portrait of Jesus with fine pigments, and brought
it with him to his master, King Abgar. When King Abgar saw that portrait, he received it with great joy
and placed it with great honor in one of the rooms of his palaces. Hannan the archivist told him
everything he had heard from Jesus, having put his words in writing. After Christ had ascended to heaven,
Judas Thomas sent to Abgar the apostle Addai, who was one of the seventy-two apostles.
When Addai came to the city of Edessa, he stayed at the house of Tobias son of Tobias, a Jew who was from Palestine.
News of him spread throughout the city. One of Abgar’s nobles came in and told him about Addai:
This man’s name was Abdu son of Abdu, one of the leading men who sat on Abgar’s council.
“Look, the messenger has arrived and is staying here—the one about whom Jesus wrote to you, ‘I will send you one of my disciples.’”
When Abgar heard these very things, and about the great miracles Addai was performing and the wonderful cures he was bringing about,
he considered it and became convinced that this was indeed the man about whom Jesus had written to him: “When I have ascended to heaven, I will send you one of my disciples,
and he will heal your illness.” Abgar sent for Tobias and said to him:
“I have heard that a powerful man has come and is staying in your house. Bring him up to me. Perhaps through him I may find good hope
of recovery.” Early the next day, Tobias took Addai the apostle
and brought him up to Abgar. Addai himself knew that he was being sent to him by the power of God.
When Addai went up and entered Abgar’s presence, while his nobles were standing beside you, at the very moment he entered,
a wonderful vision appeared to Abgar from Addai’s face. The instant Abgar saw that vision,
he fell down and bowed before Addai. Great astonishment seized everyone standing before him,
for they had not seen the vision that appeared to Abgar. Then Abgar said to Addai:
“You are truly a disciple of Jesus, the mighty Son of God, who wrote to me, ‘I will send you
one of my disciples for healing and life.’” Addai said to him, “Because you had already believed in the one who sent me to you,
for that very reason I was sent to you. And if you continue to believe in him, everything you trust him for will be yours.” Abgar said to him:
“I believed in him so firmly that I wanted to take an army and go and destroy those Jews who crucified him.
But out of regard for the Roman Empire I held back, because of the peace treaty I have established with our lord, Caesar Tiberius, as my forefathers did.”
Addai said to him, “Our Lord fulfilled his Father’s will. When he had fulfilled the will of the one who begot him, he was raised up to his Father
and sat with him in the glory in which he had been from eternity.” Abgar said to him, “I too believe in him and in his Father.”
Addai said to him, “Because you have believed in this way, I am laying my hand on you in the name of the one in whom you have believed.”
At the very moment he laid his hand on him, he was healed of the affliction of the illness that he had suffered for a long time.
Abgar was astonished and amazed: just as he had heard about the deeds and cures of Jesus, so Addai himself
was also healing in Jesus’ name without any medicine. Abdu son of Abdu also had gout in his feet.
He too brought his feet near him, and Addai laid his hand on them and healed him. He no longer had gout.
Throughout the whole city he also performed great healings and displayed astonishing miracles. Abgar said to him:
“Now everyone knows that you perform these wonders by the power of Jesus Christ, and we are amazed at your deeds.
So I ask you to tell us about his coming and about the wonders and how they happened,
and about his glorious power and the wonders that we have heard he performed,
which you yourself witnessed along with the rest of your companions.” Addai said to him: “I will not cease proclaiming this, because for this purpose
I was indeed sent here: to speak and teach everyone who wishes to believe as you do. Tomorrow gather the whole city for me,
and I will sow the word of life in it through the message I proclaim before you: about Christ’s coming and how it happened,
and about his glorious power, why and how he laid it aside, and about his power and his astonishing deeds,
and about the glorious mysteries of his coming, of which he spoke in the world, and about the certainty of his proclamation,
how and why he made himself small and humbled his exalted divinity in the body he took on,
and was crucified and descended to the realm of the dead, and broke through the barrier that had never before been breached,
and brought the dead to life through his death, and descended alone and ascended with many to his glorious Father,
with whom he had been from eternity in one exalted divinity.” Abgar commanded
that silver and gold be given to Addai. Addai said to him: “How can we accept anything that is not ours,
when we have left behind even what was ours, as our Lord commanded us, so that we should have neither purses nor bags?
Carrying crosses on our shoulders, we were commanded to proclaim his good news throughout all creation—
he at whose crucifixion all creation was shaken and suffered, a crucifixion endured for our sake, for the salvation of all humanity.”
He recounted before King Abgar, his officials and nobles, and Augustina, Abgar’s mother,
and before Shalmat, daughter of Mithridates, Abgar’s wife, the signs of our Lord, his wonders, and the glorious miracles he performed,
and his divine victories, his ascension to his Father, and how they received powers and authority at the time when he ascended.
By that very power he had healed Abgar and Abdu son of Abdu, the second-ranking man in his kingdom. He also recounted how he made known to them that he would be revealed at the end of time,
at the consummation of all created things, and the revival and resurrection that is to come for all humanity,
and the separation that will take place between the lambs and the goats, and between believers and unbelievers. He said to them:
“Because the gate of life is narrow and the way of truth is difficult, true believers are few.
And because unbelief is Satan’s delight, there are many liars who lead those who see them astray.”
For if it were not because a good outcome awaits faithful people, our Lord would not have come down from heaven
and undergone birth and the suffering of death. Nor would he have sent us ourselves to be his heralds
and messengers of good news. And the things we saw and heard from him, which he did and taught,
we confidently proclaim before everyone, so that we may not wrong the truth of his good news. And not only these things,
but also the things that happened in his name after his ascension we make known and proclaim. Now I will tell you
what happened and took place among people who, like you, believed in Christ, that he is the Son of the living God.
Protonice, the wife of Claudius Caesar, whom Tiberius had made second in command of his kingdom when he went to fight the Spaniards who had rebelled against him—
this woman, while Simon, one of the disciples, was in the city of Rome, saw the signs and wonders
and astonishing miracles that he performed in the name of Christ. She renounced the pagan religion of her ancestors, which she had followed,
and the pagan idols she had worshiped. She believed in and worshiped Christ our Lord, and [?] with those who accompanied Simon.
She held him in great honor. After this, she wished to see Jerusalem as well
and the places where our Lord's miracles had taken place. She eagerly set out and went down from Rome to Jerusalem,
with her two sons and her virgin daughter. As she was entering Jerusalem, there came out
the city to meet her. They received her with great honor, as a queen, the mistress of the great land of the Romans.
Now James, who had been appointed leader and overseer in the church that had been built for us there, heard why she had come there, and he arose and went to her.
He went in to see her where she was staying, in the great palace belonging to the royal household of King Herod.
When she saw him, she welcomed him with great joy, just as she had Simon Peter.
He too showed her healings and miracles, like Simon. She said to him, “Show me Golgotha, where Christ was crucified,
and the wood of his cross, on which he was hung by the Jews, and the tomb in which he was laid.” James said to her,
“All three of these things that Your Majesty wishes to see are under the control of the Jews. They are the ones who hold them,
and they do not allow us to go and pray there before Golgotha and the tomb. Nor are they willing to give us the wood of his cross.
And not only this, but they also persecute us relentlessly, so that we may not spread the good news and preach in the name of Christ.
And many times they even imprison us.” When she heard these things,
the queen immediately gave orders, and they brought before her Onias son of Annas the priest,
and Gedaliah son of Caiaphas, and Judas son of Abed-Shalom, the leaders and officials of the Jews. And she said,
to them: “Hand over Golgotha, the tomb, and the wood of the cross to James and those who follow him.
Let no one prevent them from ministering there according to their customary service.” When she had given these instructions to the priests,
she got up to go and see those places, and also to hand over that place to James himself and those who were with him.
Afterward she entered the tomb and found three crosses inside it:
one belonging to our Lord, and two belonging to the robbers who had been crucified with him, on his right and on his left. At that very time, when she entered the tomb with her children,
at that very moment her virgin daughter fell down and died, without pain, without illness, and without any cause of death.
When the queen saw that her daughter had died suddenly, she knelt down and prayed inside the tomb, saying in her prayer:
“God, who gave his life to death for all humanity, was crucified in this place, was laid in this tomb, and, as God who gives life to all, rose and raised many with him:
do not let the Jews who crucified you hear of this, or the misguided pagans whose images, carved idols, and pagan objects of worship I have renounced,
and look at me in mockery and say, ‘All this happened to her because she renounced the gods she used to worship and confessed Christ, whom she had not
known, and went to honor the place of his tomb and crucifixion.’ And if I, my Lord, am not worthy to be heard because I worshiped created things instead of you,
have mercy for the sake of your worshipful name, so that it may not be blasphemed in this place, as they blasphemed you at your crucifixion.”
While she was saying these things in her prayer and repeating them in the anguish of her crying before everyone who was there,
her eldest son approached her and said to her, “Listen to what I say before Your Majesty. This is what I think in my mind and in my thoughts:
this sudden death of my sister has not happened without a purpose. Rather, this is a marvelous event through which God will be glorified,
not so that his name should be blasphemed, as those who heard about this supposed. Look, we have entered the tomb and found three crosses in it,
and we do not know which of them is the cross on which Christ was hung. Through the death of this sister of mine,
we can see and learn which is Christ’s cross. For Christ does not neglect those who believe in him and seek him.”
Although Queen Protonice was deeply grieved at that time, she recognized in her mind
that her son had said these things wisely, rightly, and correctly. She took one of the crosses in her hands
and placed it on the body of her daughter, which lay before her. She said in her prayer, “God, who performed
marvelous miracles in this place, as we have heard and believed: if this cross is yours, my Lord, and on it your humanity was hung by insolent men,
show the mighty and powerful strength of your divinity, which dwelt within your humanity. Let this daughter of mine live and rise, and let your name be glorified through her
as her soul returns into her body. Let those who crucified you be put to shame, and let those who worship you rejoice.” After saying this, she waited a long time.
Afterward she took that cross off her daughter’s body and placed another one on it. Again she said in her prayer:
God, at whose command the worlds and all created things stand, who desires life for all people who turn to him, and who does not neglect the prayer of those who seek him:
“If this cross is yours, my Lord, show the power of your victories, as you always do, so that this daughter of mine may live and rise.
“Let the pagans who worship your creatures instead of you be put to shame, and let the faithful and true give thanks, their mouths opened to praise you
“before those who deny you.” After this she waited for a long [?], and took the second cross off her daughter.
She took the third cross and laid it on her daughter. As she was about to raise her eyes to heaven and open her mouth in prayer,
at that very moment, in the blink of an eye, when that cross touched her daughter's body, her daughter came to life.
She suddenly stood up and praised God, who had brought her to life through his cross. When Queen Protonice saw how her daughter had come to life,
she was shaken and greatly astonished. In her astonishment she praised Christ and believed in him,
that he is the Son of the living God. Her son said to her, “You see, my lady, if this had not happened today,
“we might have left behind this cross of Christ, through which my sister came to life, and taken
“and honored the cross of one of those murderous robbers. But now we have seen and rejoiced, and Christ has been glorified through doing this.”
She took Christ's cross and gave it to James, so that it would be kept with great honor.
She ordered a large and splendid building to be built over Golgotha, where he had been crucified, and over the tomb in which he had been laid,
so that these places would be honored, and there would be a meeting place there for prayer and an assembly for worship.
When the queen saw all the people of the city who had gathered to witness this event, she gave orders
that her daughter should go with her openly, without the covering befitting royal dignity, to the royal palace where she was staying,
so that everyone might see her and praise God. But the Jews and pagans who had rejoiced and been glad at the beginning of this affair became
deeply saddened at its outcome. For they sighed, wishing this had not happened, because they saw that, on account of it,
many had come to believe in Christ. They were especially saddened because they saw that many signs were taking place in his name after her departure,
more than those that had taken place before his ascension. News of this event also reached distant lands,
and also my fellow apostles, who were proclaiming Christ. There was peace in the churches of Jerusalem and the cities around it.
Those who had not seen this, together with those who had seen it, praised God. As the queen traveled up from Jerusalem to the city of Rome,
in every city she entered, people crowded together to see her daughter. When she entered Rome,
she recounted before Claudius Caesar all these things that had happened. When Caesar heard,
he ordered all the Jews to leave the land of Italy. Throughout that whole land, many people were speaking about this event.
This event had also been recounted before Simon Peter. So everything that our fellow apostles do,
we proclaim before everyone, so that those who do not know may also hear what Christ openly does through our hands,
so that our Lord may be praised by everyone. I have recounted these things before you so that you may know and understand how great is the faithfulness
of Christ toward those who truly follow him. Now James, the leader of the church in Jerusalem, who had seen that event with his own eyes,
had written it down and sent it to my fellow apostles in the cities of their regions. And those apostles, too,
write and inform James of everything Christ does through their hands. These accounts are read before the entire congregation of the church.
When King Abgar heard these things—he and Augustina his mother, and Shalmat daughter of Mehrdat, and Pacorus and Abdshemesh,
and Shamashgram and Abdu and Azi and Bar Kalba, together with the rest of their companions—they rejoiced greatly, and all of them praised God
and confessed Christ. King Abgar said to Addai, “I want everything we have heard from you today, as well as the other things,
to be spoken by you openly before the whole city, so that everyone may hear the proclamation of the good news of Christ that you teach us,
and may find rest and be established in the teaching you give us. Then many will understand that I was right to believe in Christ
in the letter I sent him. They will know that he is God, the Son of God, and that you are his true and faithful disciple,
and that you demonstrate his glorious power through deeds before those who wish to believe in him.” After that day,
Abgar commanded Abdu son of Abdu, who had been healed of the severe pain in his feet,
to send a herald to proclaim throughout the whole city that all the people should gather,
men and women, at the place called Beth Tabara, in the spacious area at the house of Avida son of Abdnehad,
to hear the teaching of Addai the apostle: how he taught, in whose name he healed,
and by what power he performed these signs and worked these wonders. For when he had healed King Abgar,
only the nobles who stood before him had seen him heal the king by the word of Christ—
the king whom many physicians had been unable to heal, but whom a stranger had healed through faith in Christ.
When the whole city had gathered, men and women, as the king had commanded, there stood there
Avida and Labbu, Haphsai and Bar Kalba, Labubna and Hasrun and Shamashgram, together with their companions of the same rank,
the king’s chiefs and nobles, all the officers and soldiers, the craftsmen, the Jews,
the pagans who were in this city, and the strangers from the regions of Nisibis and Harran,
and the rest of the inhabitants of this whole region of Mesopotamia. They were all standing there.
to hear the teaching of Addai, about whom they had heard that he was a disciple of Jesus, who had been crucified
in Jerusalem, and that he performed healings in his name. Addai began to speak to them as follows: “Listen, all of you, and understand
what I say before you. I am not a physician who uses medicines and roots according to human skill,
but I am a disciple of Jesus Christ, the physician of afflicted souls and the Savior who gives the life to come,
the Son of God, who came down from heaven, put on a body, and became human. He gave himself and was crucified for all humanity.
When he was hung on the wood, the sun grew dark in the sky. And when he had entered the tomb,
he rose and came out of the tomb with many others. Those who were guarding the tomb did not see how he came out of the tomb.
The watchers on high were the heralds who announced the good news of his resurrection. If he had not willed it, he would not have died,
because he is the Lord of death, which carries people away. And if it had not pleased him, he would not have put on a body either, since he himself is the body's maker.
For the same will that brought him down to birth from a virgin also brought him down to the suffering of death
and humbled the greatness of his exalted divinity—he who had been with his Father from eternity and forever.
The prophets of old spoke of him through their mysteries and portrayed images of his birth and suffering,
his resurrection, his ascension to his Father, and his sitting at the right hand. And now he is worshiped by those above and those below,
he who has been worshiped from eternity. For although his appearance was human, his power, knowledge, and authority are God's.
As he himself said to us, ‘Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God who is in him glorifies him,’ through mighty deeds and wonders
and through his honor at the right hand. His body is the pure purple robe of his glorious divinity, through which we were able to look upon his hidden lordship.
This Jesus Christ, then, is the one we proclaim and announce as good news, and together with him we glorify his Father.
We exalt and worship the Spirit of his divinity, because this is what he commanded us: to baptize and grant forgiveness to those who believe,
in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. The prophets before us also said this: ‘The Lord our God has sent us, and his Spirit.’
If I say anything that is not written in the prophets, let the Jews who stand among you and listen to me refuse to accept it.
And if I invoke the name of Christ over those who have pains and diseases, and they are not healed through this glorious name,
let those who worship the work of their own hands refuse to believe. But if the things we say are written in the Scriptures and the prophets,
and powers to heal their illnesses are found and demonstrated among the sick, let no one look upon us without examining
the faith we proclaim: that God was crucified for all humanity.
And if there are any who are unwilling to be persuaded by these words of ours, let them come forward to us.
Let them disclose to us what their thinking is, so that, in keeping with the sickness of their minds, we may offer healing medicine to cure their wound.
For although you were not nearby at the time of Christ’s suffering, you nevertheless saw it in the sun that grew dark.
Learn and understand the great calamity that occurred at the time of his crucifixion—the one whose good news has spread throughout the whole earth—
through the signs that his disciples, our companions, perform throughout the whole earth. Those who were Hebrews and knew only the Hebrew language in which they were born—
look, today they speak in every language, so that those far away may hear and believe like those nearby.
For the one who confused the languages of the arrogant in this region before us is himself teaching today through our hands
the faith of truth and certainty, through lowly and poor people from Galilee in Palestine. For I too, whom you see,
am from Paneas, from the place where the Jordan River flows out. And I was chosen along with my companions to be
a herald of this good news. Through it, look, the regions everywhere resound with the glorious name of Christ, who is worthy of worship.
Therefore, let none of you harden his mind against the truth or distance his thinking from what is certain.
Do not be taken captive by thoughts of destructive error, which are full of the despair of bitter death.
Do not cling to the evil customs of your ancestors’ paganism and distance yourselves from the true and certain life that is in Christ.
For those who believe in him are considered faithful before him, the one who came down to us in his mercy
to abolish from the earth the sacrifices of paganism and the libations of idolatry, so that created things would no longer be worshiped,
but that we might worship him and his Father, together with his Holy Spirit. For, as my Lord commanded me, look, I am proclaiming and announcing the good news.
Look, I am laying his silver on the table before you, and I am sowing the seed of his word in everyone’s ears. As for those who wish to receive it,
the good reward for their confession is theirs. As for those who are not persuaded, I shake the dust from my feet against them, as my Lord told me.
Therefore, my beloved, turn back from evil ways and hateful deeds, and turn to him with a good and upright will,
just as he turned toward you in his mercy and his abundant compassion. And do not be like the generations
of old that have passed away, who, because they had hardened their minds against the fear of God, received punishment openly,
so that they might be disciplined, and those coming after them might tremble and be afraid. For the whole purpose of our Lord’s coming into the world was
to teach us and show us that at the end of creation there will be a resurrection for all human beings.
At that time their conduct will be depicted in their own persons, and their bodies will become scrolls for the writings of justice.
There will be no one there who cannot read, because everyone will read what is written in his own book on that day,
and will keep the account of his deeds on the fingers of his hands. Thus even the uneducated will know the new writing of a new language.
And no one says to his neighbor, “Read this to me,” because one teaching and one doctrine reign over all humanity.
Let this thought, then, be pictured before your eyes, and do not let it pass from your minds, because even if it passes from your minds,
it does not pass from justice. Ask God for mercy, that he may forgive you the hateful denial involved in your paganism,
because you abandoned the one who created you on the face of the earth, who sends down his rain and makes his sun rise upon you, and instead of him you worshiped his works.
For the idols and carved images of paganism, and everything that is a created thing on which you rely
and which you worship—if they had perception and understanding,
instead of your worshiping and honoring them, they themselves ought to be grateful to you,
because you carved and fashioned them, and secured them, fastening them with nails so that they would not move.
For if created things were aware of the honors you pay them, they would rebuke you, crying out to you,
“Do not worship your fellow creatures, who are made and created like you!” For created things were not made to be worshiped,
but to worship their Creator and praise the one who created them. And just as his goodness is rejected here by the insolent,
so his justice will call the deniers to account there. For I see that this city
is deeply steeped in paganism directed against God. Who is this Nebo, the manufactured idol that you worship, and Bel, whom you honor?
For look, some among you worship the daughter of Nikkal, like your neighbors the people of Harran, and Atargatis, like the people of Mabbug, and the eagle, like the Arabs,
and the sun and moon, like the rest of the others who are like you. Do not be captivated by the rays of the heavenly lights or by the shining star.
For everyone who worships created things is cursed before God. For even though some created things are seemingly greater than their companions,
they are nevertheless fellow creatures of their companions, as I told you. For this is a bitter disease for which there is no cure:
that things made should worship things made, and that created things should praise their fellow creatures.
For just as they cannot subsist by their own power, but only by the power of the one who created them,
so they cannot be worshiped alongside him or honored alongside him. For there is blasphemy in both cases:
against created things when they are worshiped, and against the Creator when created things, which are foreign to the nature of his being, are associated with him.
For all the prophecy of the prophets, and our preaching after the prophets, is this: that created things must not be worshiped alongside the Creator,
and that human beings must no longer be harnessed under the yoke of destructive paganism. Yet it is not because created things are visible that I say they must not be worshiped.
Rather, everything that has been made is a created thing, whether visible or invisible. It is bitter wickedness
to give it the glorious name of divinity. For we do not, as you do, proclaim and worship created things.
but the Lord of created things. For the shaking that shook them at the cross itself testifies that everything that is made
hangs and stands by the power of its Maker, who existed before the ages and created things, whose nature cannot be comprehended,
since his nature cannot be seen. Together with his Father he is acclaimed as holy in the highest heavens, because he is Lord and has been God from eternity.
This is our teaching everywhere and in every region. This is how we have been commanded to proclaim it to those who listen to us,
not by force, but through the teaching of truth and the power of God. And the signs that take place
in his name bear witness that our faith is true and trustworthy. Be persuaded, then, by my words,
and accept what I have said and am saying before you. So that I may not be held accountable for your deaths, look, I am giving you ample warning.
Receive my words attentively, and do not neglect them. Come near to me, you who are far from Christ, and become close to Christ.
Instead of the sacrifices and libations of error, offer him sacrifices of thanksgiving from now on.
But what is this great altar that you have built in the middle of this city, on which those who come and go pour out libations to demons
and sacrifice to evil spirits? Even if you do not know the Scriptures, does not nature itself, through what can be seen of it, teach you
that your idols have eyes but do not see? And you, who see with your eyes, because you do not understand,
have yourselves become like them, neither seeing nor hearing. In vain you pour out your empty words
into deaf ears. Yet they are not to blame for not hearing, because they are by nature deaf and silent.
But the blame, in which justice is contained, belongs to you, because you are unwilling to understand,
even through what you see. For the darkness of error spread over your minds does not allow you to acquire the heavenly light
that is the understanding of knowledge. Flee, then, from things made and created, as I told you, which are called gods in name alone,
although they are not gods by nature. Draw near to the one who is God by nature, from eternity and forever.
He is not something made like your idols, nor something created and fashioned like the images in which you boast.
For although he put on this body, he was God with his Father. For the created things that were shaken at his killing and trembled at the suffering of his death
themselves testify that he is the one who created them. For the earth did not quake on behalf of a human being, but on behalf of the one who had spread out the earth upon the waters.
Nor was the sun darkened at the cross on behalf of a human being, but on behalf of the one who had made the great lights.
Nor were the upright and righteous raised to life through a human being, but through the one who had given death its authority in the beginning.
Nor were the door panels of the Jews’ temple torn from end to end because of a human being, but because of the one who had said to them, “Look, your house is left desolate.”
For look, if those who crucified him had not known that he was the Son of God, there would not have been the destruction of their city
They were preaching. Nor were they bringing woes upon themselves. For even if they had wanted to neglect this confession,
the terrible torments inflicted at that time would not have allowed them. For look, even some of the children of those who crucified him

have today become heralds and preachers of the good news, together with the apostles, my companions, throughout the whole land of Palestine, among the Samaritans, and throughout the land of the Philistines.
The idols of paganism are despised, and the cross of Christ is honored. Nations and created beings acknowledge the God who became a human being.
If, then, while Jesus our Lord was on earth, you believed in him as the Son of God,
and before you heard the message of his proclamation, you acknowledged him as God, now that he has ascended to his Father,
and you have seen the signs and wonders taking place in his name, and have heard the message of his good news with your own ears, let none of you doubt in your mind,
so that the promise of the blessing he sent you may be fulfilled for you: “Blessed are you who have believed in me without seeing me.
And because you have believed in me in this way, the city in which you live will be blessed, and no enemy will ever rule over it.”
Therefore, do not turn away from faith in him. For you have heard and seen the things that bear witness to faith in him: that he is the Son who is worshiped,
and he is the God who is glorified, and he is the victorious King, and he is the mighty Power. Through true faith in him a person can acquire
the eye of true understanding and perceive that everyone who worships created beings is overtaken by the wrath of justice.
For everything we say before you, we say according to what we have received from the gift of our Lord.
We teach you and show you how to put your lives in order, so that you do not destroy your souls through the error of paganism.
For the heavenly light has dawned upon creation. He is the one who chose the ancient fathers, the righteous, and the prophets,
and spoke with them through the revelation of the Holy Spirit. For he is the God of the Jews who crucified him.
And the misguided pagans worship him, even without knowing it, because there is no other God in heaven or on earth.
Look, thanksgiving rises to him from the four corners of the earth. So now your ears have heard something you had never heard,
and your eyes now see something you had never seen before. Therefore, do not deny what you have heard and seen.
Put away the rebellious mindset of your ancestors, and free yourselves from the yoke of sin that rules over you
through libations and sacrifices before carved idols. Be concerned about your lives that are being lost, and about
your futile bowing of the head. Acquire a new mind, one that worships the Maker rather than what is made, one in which the image of truth and reality is portrayed,
of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, as you believe and are baptized in the three glorious names. For this is our teaching and our proclamation.
For the truth of Christ is not believed through a multitude of words. And you who wish to obey Christ know
that I have repeated my words before you many times, so that you may learn and understand what you are hearing.
And we will rejoice in this, like a farmer in his blessed field, and our God will be glorified by your repentance and return to him.
And while you gain life through this, we too, who counsel you to do this, will not be deprived of its blessed reward.
And because I am confident that you will be blessed soil, according to the will of the Lord Christ, therefore, instead of the dust from my feet, which we were told
to shake off against a town that does not receive our words, today I have shaken out the words of my lips at the entrance to your ears.
In them are portrayed the coming of Christ, both the one that has taken place and the one that is yet to take place, and the resurrection and restoration to life of all humanity,
and the separation that will take place between believers and unbelievers, and the terrible punishment reserved for those who do not know God, and the blessed promise
of the joys to come, which those who have believed in Christ will receive, who have worshiped him and his exalted Father,
and have acknowledged him and the Spirit of his divinity. And now we ought to conclude our present discourse. Let those who have received the word of Christ remain with us,
as well as those who wish to join us in prayer. Then let them go to their homes.
And Addai the apostle rejoiced at this, because he saw that most of the city's population had remained with him,
and that those who had not remained at that time were few. Even these few, after a few days,
accepted his words and believed in the good news of his proclamation of Christ. And when Addai the apostle had said these things
before the whole town of Edessa, and King Abgar saw that the whole city rejoiced in his teaching,
men and women alike, and were saying to him, “Christ, who sent you to us, is true and trustworthy,” he too rejoiced greatly at this,
praising God because, just as he had heard about Christ from Hannan his archivist, so he now saw the marvelous miracles
that Addai the apostle was performing in Christ's name. King Abgar himself also said to Addai the apostle, “Just as I wrote
to Christ in my letters to him, and just as he himself wrote to me, and as I have received from you yourself today,
so I will believe all the days of my life, and I will remain steadfast in these things, taking pride in them,
because I know that there is no other power in whose name these signs and wonders occur,
except through the power of Christ, whom you proclaim truly and faithfully. And from now on I will worship him,
I and my son Ma'nu, and Augustin and Queen Shalmat. And now, wherever you wish, build a church, a meeting place
for those who have believed and do believe your words. And as your Lord has commanded you, conduct the ministry confidently at the appointed times.
And as for those who serve with you as teachers of this good news, I am prepared to give them generous gifts,
so that they will have no other occupation besides the ministry. And whatever you need for the expenses of the building,
I will give you without requiring an accounting. Your word shall have authority and rule in this town, and no one else's.”
You used to enter freely into the glorious palace of my kingdom. And when Abgar came down
the king, to his royal palace, he rejoiced, together with his nobles: Abdu, Garmi, Shamshagram, Abubi, and Mihrdat,
along with the rest of their companions, at everything their eyes saw and their ears heard. And with joy in their hearts,
they too praised God, who had turned their minds toward himself, as they renounced the paganism in which they had persisted
and professed the gospel of Christ. And while Addai was building a church, they offered votive gifts and offerings in it,
both they and the people of the city. There they ministered all the days of their lives. And there approached Addai
Awida and Bar-Kalba, who were chiefs and officials and wore the king’s white garments.
They questioned Addai about the story of Christ, asking him to tell them how, although he was God,
he appeared to them as a human being, and how they had been able to look at him.
He satisfied them all on this matter, concerning everything their eyes had seen and everything their ears had heard from him.
He recounted before them everything the prophets had said about him, and they received his words gladly and with faith. There was no one who stood
against him, for the mighty deeds he performed did not allow anyone to stand against him.
But Shwida and Abed-Nebo, the chief priests of this city, together with their companions Piroz and Danku, when they saw the signs he was performing,
ran and tore down the altars on which they used to sacrifice before Nebo and Bel, their gods,
except for the great altar in the middle of the city. They cried out, saying, “Truly, this man is a disciple of that skilled and glorious master!”
For they had heard about everything he had done in the land of Palestine. And all those who believed in Christ
Addai received and baptized in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
Those who had worshiped stones and wood sat at his feet, learning and being restored
from the affliction of the madness of paganism. Even the Jews who knew the Law and the Prophets, who sold fine fabrics,
were themselves persuaded, became disciples, and confessed that Christ is the Son of the living God.
Neither King Abgar nor Addai the apostle compelled anyone to believe by force
in Christ. For without anyone’s coercion, the compelling power of the signs urged many to believe in him.
And they received his teaching with love throughout this whole land of Mesopotamia and all the regions around it.
Now Aggai, who made the king’s silks and necklaces, and Palut, Abshlama, and Barsamya, together with the rest of their companions, followed Addai the apostle.
He received them and made them his partners in the ministry, as they read the Old and New Testaments and the Prophets.
And they studied the Acts of the Apostles every day, while he carefully instructed them:
“Let your bodies be pure and your persons holy, as is fitting for people who stand before the altar of God.
And keep far away from false oaths, from wicked murder, and from false testimony, which is entangled with adultery;
and from sorcerers, on whom there is no mercy; from soothsayers, diviners, and necromancers; and from astrological destinies and horoscopes,
in which the misguided Chaldeans boast; and from the stars and signs of the zodiac, in which fools trust.
Keep unjust favoritism far from you, along with bribes and gifts through which the innocent are condemned. And alongside this ministry
to which you have been called, let there be no other occupation for you. For the Lord is the one you serve in your ministry all the days of your lives.
Be diligent in giving the seal of baptism, and do not love the profits of this world.
Hear legal cases with justice and truth, and do not become a stumbling block to the blind,
lest through you the name of the one who opened the eyes of the blind, as we have seen, be blasphemed. Therefore, let everyone who sees you
recognize that you live in accordance with everything you proclaim and teach.” And they ministered with him in the church that Addai himself had built
at the word and command of King Abgar. They were supported from the property of the king and his nobles, and they brought some of it to the house of God
and some for the support of the poor. A great multitude gathered day after day and came to the prayers of the service
and to the Old Testament and the New, the Diatessaron. They believed in the resurrection of the dead and buried their departed in the hope of resurrection.
They celebrated the festivals of the church at their appointed times and faithfully attended the church vigil every day.
They performed charitable deeds for the sick and the healthy, according to Addai’s teaching to them.
Churches were being built around the city, and many received from him the laying on of hands for the priesthood.
Thus even people from the East crossed into Roman territory disguised as merchants, to see the signs that Addai was performing.
Those among them who became disciples received from them the laying on of hands for the priesthood. And in their own country of Assyria,
they made disciples of their fellow countrymen and secretly established houses of prayer there, for fear of those who worshiped and honored fire.
When Narses, king of the Assyrians, heard about these things that Addai the apostle was doing, he sent word to King Abgar:
“Either send me that man who performs these signs among you, so that I may see him and hear his message,
or send me an account of everything you have seen him do in your city.” And Abgar wrote to Narses and told him the whole account of Addai’s story,
from beginning to end. He left nothing unwritten to him. When Narses heard what had been written to him,
he was amazed and astonished. But King Abgar, because he was unable to cross into Roman territory,
And he would go to Palestine and kill the Jews because they had crucified Christ. He wrote a letter
and sent it to Tiberius Caesar, writing in it as follows: “King Abgar to our lord Tiberius Caesar: greetings.
Although I know that nothing is hidden from Your Majesty, I am writing to inform your great and awesome authority
that the Jews under your rule who live in the land of Palestine assembled and crucified Christ, though he had committed no offense deserving death.
He had performed signs and wonders before them and shown them mighty miracles and signs,
even raising the dead for them. And at the time when they crucified him, the sun grew dark and the earth shook,
and all created things trembled. By this deed, as far as it depended on them, all creation and its inhabitants were brought to an end.
And now Your Majesty knows what punishment you should decree against the Jewish people who did these things.” Tiberius Caesar wrote
and sent a letter to King Abgar. He wrote to him as follows: “I received the letter expressing your loyalty to me, and it was read before me,
concerning what the Jews had done in the crucifixion. Pilate the governor also wrote and informed my prefect, Ulbinus,
about these things of which you wrote to me. But because the war with the people of Spain, who have rebelled against me, is ongoing
at this time, I have been unable to investigate this matter. But I am prepared, once I have peace,
to pass judgment according to the law against the Jews who acted unlawfully. For this reason, as for Pilate, whom I had appointed governor there,
I have sent another man in his place and dismissed him in disgrace, because he departed from the law and did what the Jews wanted,
and crucified Christ to please the Jews. According to what I hear about them, he should have been honored instead of being crucified to death,
and he deserved to be worshiped by them, especially since they saw with their own eyes everything he did.
But you, in keeping with your loyalty to me and the faithful covenant of you and your ancestors, did well to write to me in this way.”
King Abgar received Aristides, who had been sent to him by Tiberius Caesar.
He sent him back with gifts of honor befitting the one who had sent him to him. He departed from Edessa
and went to Ticnutha, where Claudius, the emperor’s deputy, was staying. From there he went on to Artica,
where Tiberius Caesar was staying. Gaius, meanwhile, was guarding the regions surrounding Caesar himself.
Aristides himself also recounted before Tiberius the miracles that Addai had performed before King Abgar.
When he had peace from the war, he sent and had some of the Jewish leaders in Palestine killed.
When King Abgar heard this, he rejoiced greatly that the Jews had received the punishment they deserved.
And some years after Addai the apostle had built the church in Edessa and furnished it with everything it needed,
He made disciples of a great many people in the city, and also in other villages, both far and near.
He built churches, completed and adorned them, and appointed deacons and elders in them.
He taught in them those who read the Scriptures, and he taught the orders of worship, both inside and outside. After all these things,
he fell ill with the illness through which he would depart from this world. He summoned Aggai before the whole congregation of the church,
brought him forward, and made him leader and overseer in his place. He made Palut, who was a deacon, an elder.
He made Abshlama, who was a scribe, a deacon. And when the nobles and leaders were gathered and standing beside him—
Bar-Kalba, Bar-Zatti, Marihab son of Bar-Shamash, Sennac son of Avida, and Peroz son of Patric, with the rest
of their companions—Addai the apostle said to them, “All of you who are listening to me know and bear witness
that I conducted myself among you in accordance with everything I preached and taught you, which you heard from me. You also saw it in my deeds.
For our Lord commanded us that we should put into practice before everyone what we proclaim in words before the people.
And in accordance with the orders and laws established in Jerusalem, by which my fellow apostles also conduct themselves, so you too
must not depart from them or take anything away from them, just as I also conducted myself among you by them.
I did not turn aside from them to the right or to the left, so that I would not be excluded from the promised life reserved for those who conduct themselves by them.
Therefore, be attentive to this ministry that you hold. Continue in it with fear and trembling,
serving every day. Do not carry out this ministry with contemptible habits, but with the discernment of faith.
Let the praises of Christ never cease from your mouths, and let no laziness come near you in faithfully observing the appointed times.
Guard the truth that you hold, the true teaching that you have received, and the inheritance of life
that I entrust to you. For you will be held accountable for it before the judgment seat of Christ, when he settles accounts with the shepherds and overseers,
and when he receives his money from the merchants with the interest of their profits. For he is the King’s Son, who went away to receive a kingdom and will return.
He will come and bring about the resurrection of all humanity. Then he will sit on the throne of righteousness and judge the dead and the living, as he told us.
Do not let the hidden eye of your mind close to the heights above, lest your stumbling increase on the road where there are no stumbling blocks,
nor any hateful straying along its paths. Seek out the lost and attend to those who have strayed,
and rejoice over those who are found. Bind up the injured and guard the well-fed,
for you will be held accountable for Christ’s sheep. Do not look for fleeting honor.
For a shepherd who looks to be honored by his flock leaves his flock in a very bad state. Take great care of the young lambs.
that their angels see the face of the invisible Father. And do not be a stumbling stone before the blind.
Instead, make the road and path easy in difficult country, among the Jews who crucified him and the pagans who have gone astray. For it is only with these two
sides that you have a battle to fight, to show the truth of the faith you hold. Even when you are silent, your modest and dignified appearance
will fight on your behalf against those who hate truth and love falsehood. Do not humiliate the poor in front of the rich.
For the bitter scourge of their poverty is enough for them. Do not be carried away by Satan's evil thoughts,
lest you be stripped naked of the faith in which you are clothed. For denying the faith is easier than keeping it,
just as sin is easier than righteousness. Therefore beware of those who crucified him, and do not become their friends,
lest you be held accountable along with them for the blood of Christ that fills their hands. You know and bear witness that everything we say and teach concerning Christ
is written in the book of the prophets and is kept among them. Their words bear witness to our teaching
about Christ's judgment, suffering, resurrection, and ascension. They do not know that when they stand against us, they stand against the words of the prophets.
Just as they persecuted the prophets during their lives, so now, after their deaths, they persecute the truth written in the prophets.
Beware also of the pagans, who worship the sun and the moon, Bel and Nebo, and the rest whom they call
gods, although they are not gods by nature. Flee from them, therefore, because they worship created and manufactured things.
As you have heard before, the whole purpose of our Lord's coming into the world was that created things should no longer be worshiped and honored.
For they exist by their Maker's command, and whenever he wishes, he dissolves and abolishes them, and they become as though they did not exist.
For the same will that created these things freed human beings from the yoke of the pagan worship of created things.
For you know that anyone who worships the king's servants along with the king meets death by the sword because of his worship.
Do not investigate hidden things or inquire into secret things written in the holy Scriptures that you hold.
Do not pass judgment on the words of the prophets. Remember and recognize that they were spoken by the Spirit of God. Whoever finds fault with the prophets
finds fault with and judges the Spirit of God. May you be spared this! For the ways of the Lord are straight,
and the righteous walk in them without stumbling, while unbelievers stumble in them, because they lack the hidden eye of the hidden mind,
which has no need of questions that bring no benefit, but only harm. Remember the judgment threatened by the prophets,
and our Lord's word, which is framed in accordance with their words: that the Lord judges by fire, and by it all human beings are tested.
Therefore, like travelers and temporary residents who spend the night and set out early for their homes, so should
you regard yourselves in this world, for you are departing from here to the places that the Son went to prepare for everyone worthy of them.
The kings of the lands have their armies go ahead of them and prepare a lodging worthy of their honor. But this King of ours—
look, he himself has gone to prepare blessed chambers for his servants to dwell in. For God did not create human beings without a purpose,
but so that they would worship and praise him, here and there forever, so that, just as he does not pass away, those who praise him should not cease.
For these reasons, let even my death—for look, I am bound and lie stricken by its sickness—be regarded in your eyes as a night's sleep. And remember that through the suffering of the Son,
the death that carried human beings away has passed away and ceased, as has Satan, who leads many into sin and fights against the faithful to make them unfaithful.
Just as a farmer who puts his hand on the blade of the plow cannot keep the furrows straight ahead of him if he looks behind him,
so you too, who have been called to this gift of ministry, must be watchful, so that you are not distracted by the affairs of this world,
lest you be hindered from what you have been called to. As for the rulers and judges who approach them,
show them no favoritism in anything. But if they do wrong, rebuke
them justly, so that you may openly demonstrate your uprightness and they may be corrected,
so that they no longer conduct themselves according to their own desires. Let this be your concern all the days of your lives:
always pursue good things, while also advising others about them. For it is through these things that human beings find
their lives before God. Now the Law, the Prophets, and the Gospel, which you read every day before the people, and the letters of Paul,
which Simon Peter sent us from the city of Rome, and the Acts of the twelve apostles, which John son of Zebedee sent us from Ephesus—these are the books
you are to read in the churches of Christ. Along with these, you are not to read anything else,
since there is nothing else in which the truth you hold is written, except these books to which you hold fast in the faith to which you were called.
And our lord King Abgar and his honored nobles, who heard what I said before you today,
are able to be witnesses for me after my death that our Lord's teaching was diligently proclaimed before everyone,
and that I acquired nothing in the world besides his word. For his word was enough for me: through it I became rich, and through it I enriched many,
so that it may accompany me on this road that I am traveling, into the presence of Christ, who has sent for me, and that through it I may journey to him. You know
that I told you that all human souls that depart from this body do not die,
but live and continue to exist, and have chambers and a resting place. For the soul's understanding and knowledge do not cease,
because the image of God, who does not die, is imprinted upon it. For it is not without sensation like the body,
which does not feel the loathsome decay that comes upon it. It cannot receive reward and recompense without the body,
because the labor was not its alone, but also that of the body in which it dwelt. But the rebels who do not know God—
They repent there to no avail. But you belong to Christ, whose glorious name has been placed upon you and reigns over you.
He has set you on the path of truth, so that you may walk in it, arrive, and attain
what is promised and reserved for those who do not turn aside from him, but remain as they were called by our Lord. When he had said these words,
Addai the apostle stopped and fell silent. Then Aggai, the maker of the king’s silks, and Palut and Abshlama, together with the rest of their companions, responded
and said to Addai the apostle, “Christ, who sent you to us, is witness that you have taught us the true faith
and given us true life. Just as we have heard from you and accepted throughout this whole time that you have been with us,
so we will remain all the days of our lives. And we flee from the worship of things made and created, which
our ancestors worshiped. We do not mingle with the Jews and those who crucified him, and we will not abandon this inheritance that we have received from you.
With it we will depart from this world. And on the day of our Lord, before the judgment seat of the righteous Judge,
there he will grant us this inheritance, as you told us.” When these things had been said, King Abgar and his nobles rose,
along with all the freeborn men of his kingdom, and he went to his palace. They were all grieving over Addai because he was dying.
He sent him costly and splendid clothes in which to be buried. When Addai saw them, he sent word to him:
“During my life I have taken nothing from you, and I will not falsify in my own conduct the word of Christ, who told me, ‘Take nothing from anyone,
and acquire nothing from this world.’” Three more days after these things had been said by Addai the apostle,
and after he had heard and received from his fellow ministers their testimony to the teaching he had proclaimed, he departed from this world in the presence of all the freeborn men.
It was Thursday, the fourteenth of the month of Iyar. Great mourning and bitter sorrow over him fell upon the whole
city. It was not only the Christians who grieved over him, but also the Jews and pagans who were in this city.
King Abgar grieved over him more than anyone else, together with the nobles of his kingdom. In his distress of mind,
he disregarded and laid aside his royal dignity that day, and wept for him with sorrowful tears along with everyone else.
All the people of the city who saw him marveled at how deeply he grieved over him. With great and exceptional honor,
he accompanied him in procession and buried him, as when one of the nobles died. He laid him in a great tomb with ornamental carvings,
the one in which the members of the house of Aryu, the ancestors of King Abgar’s father, were laid. There he laid him with care,
in sorrow and great distress. All the people of the church would go there from time to time and pray earnestly.
They observed his commemoration year after year, according to the command and teaching they had received from Addai the apostle,
and according to the instruction of Aggai, who became their leader and overseer and the successor to his seat after him, through the priestly ordination he had received from him before everyone.
And he too, through the same laying on of hands that he had received from him, ordained priests
and leaders throughout this whole region of Mesopotamia. For they too, just as they had with Addai the apostle,
held firmly to his word, listened to him, and accepted him as a good and faithful heir of the apostle of the worshipful Christ.
He took neither silver nor gold from anyone, and gifts from the great did not come near him.
For instead of gold and silver, he enriched Christ’s church with the souls of believers. And the entire covenant community, both men and women,
were chaste and pure, holy and clean. They lived in celibacy and chastity, without defilement,
with vigilance and purity in their ministry, in their care for the poor, and in their visits to the sick.
For their conduct was filled with praise from those who saw them, and their way of life was clothed in praise from outsiders,
so that even the priests of [?], Nebo, and Bel constantly paid them honor because of their dignified appearance,
their truthful speech, the boldness they possessed, and their freedom, which was not yoked to greed
or held subject to blame. For everyone who saw them would run to meet them and greet them
respectfully, because their very appearance spread peace over those who saw them.
For their words of peace were spread like nets over the rebellious, as they entered the fold of truth and uprightness.
There was no one who saw them and recoiled from them, because they did nothing unjust or improper. Through these things,
they could openly proclaim their teaching to everyone. For whatever they told others and urged them to do,
they themselves demonstrated personally through their deeds. And among the hearers who saw that their deeds matched their words, without persuasion,
many became their disciples and acknowledged Christ the King, praising God, who had turned them toward himself.
Some years after the death of King Abgar, one of his rebellious sons arose, who would not be persuaded by the truth. He sent word to Aggai,
while he was sitting in the church: “Make me gold headbands, just as you used to make for my forefathers.” Aggai sent word back to him:
“I will not abandon the ministry of Christ, which was entrusted to me by Christ’s disciple, and make headbands for wickedness.”
When he saw that Aggai would not obey him, he sent someone to break his legs while he was sitting in the church teaching. And as
he was dying, he put Palut and Absalom under oath: “In this house, for the sake of whose name I am now dying, lay me down and bury me.”
And just as he had put them under oath, so they laid him inside the middle door of the church, between the men and the women.
There was great and bitter mourning throughout the whole church and the whole city over the grief and bereavement that had come upon it,
just as there had been mourning when Addai the apostle died. And because, when his legs were broken, he died suddenly and swiftly,
He had been unable to lay hands on Palut. Palut himself had gone to Antioch and had received the laying on of hands for the priesthood
from Serapion, bishop of Antioch. This same Serapion, bishop of Antioch, had himself received the laying on of hands
from Zephyrinus, bishop of the city of Antioch, through the succession of the laying on of hands for the priesthood from Simon Peter, who had received it from our Lord,
and who had been bishop there in Rome for twenty-five years, in the days of the Caesars—the one who had reigned there for thirteen years.
And just as it is customary in the kingdom of King Abgar and in all kingdoms that everything said before him is written down and placed in the archives, so also Labubna,
son of Sannaq, son of Abshaddar, the king’s scribe, had written down these things concerning Addai the apostle,
